perspective:
From Alice Lim’s perspective, she has access to:

- She is Alice Lim, a dental hygienist; Austin Moreno is her close old friend from high school. They discuss personal and professional lives and support each other. She knows he works in insurance/office work and that their career paths differ.
- She noticed Austin had become reserved or changed when work came up. She invited him for coffee and asked if things were okay at his office, telling him he could talk to her.
- She heard Austin say his work situation was “nothing really,” just “usual ups and downs,” and that he was “not sure how to handle a few things at work” and it was “complicated.” From this, she believes something specific is bothering him and suspects he may be hiding something about his job performance.
- She believes Austin may be considering a career change because of work dissatisfaction. She feels worried about his well-being and asks whether he has thought about changing careers.
- She heard Austin say he has thought about it but does not know what other paths to take, and he asks for her suggestions.
- She told Austin healthcare needs dedicated people and offered to share her experiences and connect him with contacts. He said that sounded interesting and wanted to know more.
- She senses Austin is hesitant or afraid of the unknown. She feels frustration and empathy, then tells him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and is happier. She encourages him that growth comes from leaving comfort zones and says she supports him.
- She heard Austin say Lara’s story is inspiring but he worries about risks and initial struggle. He thanked her and said her support and real success stories help.
- She offered to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. He said that would be helpful and appreciated the connections. She said she would set up a meeting next week, and he said he looked forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, she believes Austin is ready for the next steps and appreciates her help. She feels satisfaction and joy.
- She told Austin she was proud of the steps he had taken and asked how he felt. He said he felt excited, nervous, and grateful. She suggested regular check-ins; he agreed, saying it would keep him focused and that he values her perspective.

Not available to Alice: Austin’s private thoughts or motives beyond what he said, the actual hidden cause of his work issue, whether he is truly hiding job-performance problems, and any events or facts she did not observe, hear, or participate in.
